scope: Bexar County (San Antonio) and nearby Comal & Guadalupe counties: food, housing, utilities, cash assistance, transportation, plus related local health, mental health, childcare, employment, and legal services

records.name: San Antonio Food Bank Food Assistance
records.description_en: Free food at Market distributions, on-site curbside pickup, and partner pantries. Pet food is also given out when available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people and families facing food insecurity in Southwest Texas. Call Client Services to find a distribution near you.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food / FRESH TRAK tool on the Get Help page to register for a distribution near your zip code, or call Client Services at (210) 431-8326. Some events need pre-registration and give a confirmation code.
records.hours: Walk-in: Mon-Fri 8 AM-5 PM. Phone lines: Mon-Fri 8 AM-6 PM, Sat 9 AM-3 PM
records.notes: Serves 29 counties in Southwest Texas; for Comal/Guadalupe see its affiliate, the New Braunfels Food Bank. A car is not required; walk-up options exist. Main line (210) 337-3663.

records.name: SNAP and Benefits Application Help
records.description_en: Staff help you screen for, apply for, or renew SNAP, Medicaid, and other state and federal benefits. They can also answer questions about a pending SNAP case.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone who needs help applying for SNAP, Medicaid, or other benefits.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the referral form on the Get Help page and staff will contact you, call (210) 431-8326, or walk in Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM.
records.hours: Phone: Mon-Fri 8 AM-6 PM, Sat 9 AM-3 PM. Walk-in: Mon-Fri 8 AM-5 PM
records.notes: While a SNAP application is processing, the Food Bank can connect the client to food distributions.

records.name: Senior Food Box (CSFP) and Project HOPE
records.description_en: Seniors can get a free monthly box of shelf-stable groceries (CSFP) or groceries through Project HOPE. There are also farmers market vouchers for fresh produce.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For eligible seniors age 60 and older.
records.how_to_apply: Call Client Services at (210) 431-8326 to find a senior food box site near you.
records.hours: Phone: Mon-Fri 8 AM-6 PM, Sat 9 AM-3 PM
records.notes: Boxes are handed out through community partner sites.

records.name: New Braunfels Food Bank Client-Choice Pantry and Drive-Thru
records.organization: New Braunfels Food Bank (affiliate of San Antonio Food Bank)
records.description_en: A grocery-store-style pantry where you pick up to 100 pounds of shelf-stable food plus fresh produce, once every 4 weeks. Drive-thru food distributions and SNAP application help are also offered.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people and families in Comal and Guadalupe counties facing food insecurity.
records.how_to_apply: First visit: no appointment needed; come during new neighbor intake hours to register in person. Returning clients request their next appointment with the online form.
records.hours: New neighbor intake: Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri 8:30-10:45 AM and 1:00-3:15 PM; Thu 8:30-10:45 AM. Office: Mon-Sat 8 AM-5 PM
records.notes: Pantry appointments must be at least 30 days apart. Only service animals allowed in the pantry.

records.name: NBU Utility Assistance
records.organization: New Braunfels Food Bank with New Braunfels Utilities (NBU)
records.description_en: Short-term help paying a New Braunfels Utilities (NBU) bill. NBU funds the aid and the New Braunfels Food Bank takes the applications.
records.eligibility_summary_en: NBU residential customers with an active account whose household income is below 150% of the federal poverty guideline, or who have a financial emergency. Example: under $4,125 a month for a family of 4.
documents_needed: Government-issued photo ID of the account holder
NBU bill or proof you are an NBU customer
Proof of income
Optional: proof of eligibility for an emergency program
records.how_to_apply: Apply online with the Apply Now form on the NBU Utility Assistance page, or call the New Braunfels Food Bank for help applying.
records.notes: Program year Aug 1, 2026-Jul 31, 2027: up to 3 assistance payments; the 3rd requires a financial literacy or energy class. Only for NBU customers.

records.name: City of San Antonio Utility Assistance (CPS Energy bills)
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Helps pay CPS Energy utility bills for low-income households.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Household income must be at or below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines (for example $48,225 a year for 4 people). Priority goes to homes with children under 17, people with disabilities, and adults 60 and older.
documents_needed: Proof of residency for all household members
Proof of income for the last 30 days for all adults 18+
Current Social Security, disability, or unemployment letters or bank statements
CPS Energy bill and account number
Photo ID for the account holder
Last 4 digits of the account holder's Social Security number
records.how_to_apply: Gather your documents, then complete the online application. Processing can take 30 days or more.
records.address: Willie Velasquez Learning Center, 1302 N. Zarzamora St.
records.notes: Processing takes 30+ days; clients should keep paying what they can.

records.name: CPS Energy Affordability Discount Program (ADP)
records.description_en: A monthly discount on CPS Energy electric and gas bills, about $18.36 a month for customers with both services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Household income at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines, plus one of these: age 60+, a disability, life-sustaining medical equipment, children 18 or younger, or spending over 10% of income on energy.
documents_needed: Supporting documentation of income and qualifying condition
records.how_to_apply: Apply online, bring your documents to a CPS Energy Customer Service Center, or call (210) 353-2222. You must re-certify every year.
records.notes: 2026 monthly gross income limit: 1 person under $1,995; 4 people under $4,125. CPS also offers Casa Verde free weatherization, budget billing, and senior/disabled billing programs.

records.name: Residential Energy Assistance Partnership (REAP)
records.organization: CPS Energy with City of San Antonio and Bexar County
records.description_en: Credits of up to $480 a year on CPS Energy bills. You may apply twice a year.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio or Bexar County residents with income at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines who are 60+, disabled, have children under 17 at home, or need critical-care equipment.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: San Antonio or Bexar County resident

documents_needed: Proof of income
Proof of hardship
Proof of number of family members
records.how_to_apply: San Antonio residents apply with the City of San Antonio online application. Bexar County residents can call (210) 335-3666 for help.
records.notes: Online application requires an email address. The phone number is listed for Bexar County residents.

records.name: SAWS Uplift Assistance Program
records.description_en: One application gives access to 14 kinds of help with your SAWS water bill.
records.eligibility_summary_en: SAWS residential account holders who meet income limits and whose home value is $300,000 or less.
records.how_to_apply: Complete the Uplift application from the SAWS Affordability Programs page or call SAWS Customer Service.
records.notes: Exact income limits were not listed on the page. SAWS also offers payment plans and Plumbers to People repairs.

records.name: Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (CEAP)
records.organization: Community Council of South Central Texas (CCSCT)
records.description_en: Pays part of home energy bills based on your past 12 months of bills, and can help in a crisis when service is cut off or about to be. May also repair heating and cooling units.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income households up to 150% of federal poverty guidelines. Priority goes to people 60+, people with disabilities, families with children 5 or under, and those with the lowest income and highest energy costs.
documents_needed: Social Security cards for all household members
Proof of all income for the past 30 days for every member 18+
Declaration of Income Statement for adults with no income
Proof of citizenship and identity for all household members
Photo ID
records.how_to_apply: Download the 2026 application (English or Spanish), fill it out, and email it with all required documents to the office for your county. Applications missing documents will not be processed.
records.notes: CEAP provider for Comal and Guadalupe (plus 24 other counties). The CEAP phone is the program office in Jourdanton (1220 Simmons Ave); the address shown is CCSCT headquarters in Seguin. Aid limits: up to $1,800 (0-50% FPL), $1,500 (51-75%), $1,200 (76-150%). Payments go to the utility and do not cover water, sewer, trash, deposits, or fees.

records.name: Tenant-Based Rental Assistance (TBRA)
records.organization: Community Council of South Central Texas (CCSCT)
records.description_en: Help with security and utility deposits and monthly rent for up to 24 months while you take part in a self-sufficiency program.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income renters in the CCSCT service area, including Comal and Guadalupe. Extra funds are set aside for people with disabilities.
records.how_to_apply: Download the 2026 TBRA application from the Rental Assistance page and contact the Housing Assistance Program office.
records.notes: Funded by the TDHCA HOME program. Office is in Kerrville. TBRA income limit not stated on the page.

records.name: City of San Antonio Rental Assistance Program
records.organization: City of San Antonio Neighborhood & Housing Services Department
records.description_en: Up to 3 months of rent and utility help: up to $3,500 for rent and up to $1,500 for utilities, once in 12 months.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Renters inside San Antonio city limits (Council Districts 1-10) with a current lease and household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income ($56,350 for 1 person in 2026).

eligibility_rules.residency_required: City of San Antonio resident (Council Districts 1-10) with a current lease

documents_needed: Valid ID (driver's license, state ID, passport, or matricula consular)
Current lease
Proof of financial hardship in the past 12 months
Proof of income from the last 60 days
Asset documents if over $5,000
Housing provider agreement and tenant ledger
records.how_to_apply: Apply online on the second Wednesday of each month. The portal is open only from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m.
records.notes: Very short monthly application window. Also reachable at 3-1-1 or (210) 207-6000.

records.name: Eviction Prevention and Help
records.organization: City of San Antonio Neighborhood & Housing Services Department
records.description_en: Help for renters facing eviction, including guides on tenant rights and the eviction process and referrals to legal aid and rent help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio renters who are facing eviction.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 207-5910 or use the eviction help form on the city website.
records.notes: The page also lists: Bexar County Housing Authority rent/utility help (210) 225-0071; Catholic Charities Crisis Intervention (210) 226-6171; St. Vincent de Paul (210) 225-7837.

records.name: Public Housing and Housing Choice Vouchers
records.organization: Opportunity Home San Antonio (San Antonio Housing Authority)
records.description_en: Offers public housing, Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8), and affordable apartments where rent is based on income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Household income may not be more than 80% of Area Median Income (for example $80,500 for 4 people in FY2026). Applicants must meet HUD citizenship or immigration rules and pass screening.
documents_needed: Information on all adult household members for screening (citizenship/immigration, income, rental history)
records.how_to_apply: Apply online for public housing; voucher applications open only when the waitlist is open. Some affordable communities take applications directly at the property.
records.notes: Wait times: public housing 2-4 years; vouchers up to 4 years. Waitlist questions: (210) 477-6658. TTY (210) 224-7124. Text (210) 477-6055.

records.name: Haven for Hope Shelter and Services Campus
records.description_en: Homeless shelter campus. The South Campus offers low-barrier indoor sleeping, and the North Campus offers longer stays with services for people and families working toward housing.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People experiencing homelessness. South Campus: adults 18+ with proof of homelessness and ID. North Campus: Bexar County residents (12 months of the last 2 years) who agree to a housing plan, drug test, and background check.
documents_needed: Proof of homelessness (eviction notice, family statement, or receipts)
U.S. state or government-issued photo ID
North Campus: proof of Bexar County residency
Families: proof of relationship to children (birth certificates, hospital or school records)
records.how_to_apply: Walk in to the Intake building Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM, or call (210) 220-2100.
records.notes: Clients must be able to do daily living activities on their own. Intake email: intakeinfo@havenforhope.org.

records.name: SAMMinistries Rent, Utility, and Housing Help
records.description_en: Shelter, housing, and rent and utility help for people who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio families and individuals who are homeless or about to be.
records.how_to_apply: Submit a request with the online Typeform on the Get Help page. The form opens only when help slots are available.
records.notes: Limited slots; the form closes when full. For long-term re-housing the page points to 2-1-1 or the City of San Antonio Homeless Hotline (210) 207-1799.

records.name: St. Stephen's CARE Center Food Pantry and Rent/Utility Help
records.organization: Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio
records.description_en: A free client-choice food pantry with canned goods, meat, dairy, bread, fresh produce, and diapers. Case managers also help with rent and utility assistance by appointment.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in need in the San Antonio area. Eligibility details were not listed; call to ask.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 226-6178 to schedule an appointment with a case manager for rent or utility help, or call to ask about pantry visits.
records.notes: The posted Mon-Fri 9 AM-4 PM hours are for food donations; call to confirm client hours. Main Catholic Charities line: (210) 222-1294.

records.name: Battered Women & Children's Shelter
records.description_en: 24-hour emergency shelter and transitional housing for people escaping family violence, plus crisis help by phone.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults and children experiencing family violence in the San Antonio area.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline at (210) 733-8810 for crisis help and emergency shelter.
records.notes: Programs and admin line: (210) 930-3669. Do not share shelter location.

records.name: VIA Reduced Fare Program
records.description_en: Lower bus fares for seniors, children, students, people with certain disabilities, Medicare and SSDI recipients, and active-duty military. Seniors pay 25 cents weekdays 9 AM-3 PM and ride free on weekends.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Seniors 62+, children 5-13 (4 and under ride free), students, people with certain disabilities (veterans need a VA rating of 80%+), Medicare or SSDI recipients, and active-duty military.
documents_needed: Government-issued ID with date of birth
Students: proof of enrollment or paid tuition
Medicare card or SSDI award letter
Veterans: VA disability rating letter (80% or higher)
records.how_to_apply: Get a VIA Reduced Fare ID at any VIA Information Center (except Randolph Transit Center). Bring the documents for your group.
records.notes: Students 12-18 can get a free Semester Pass.

records.name: Alamo Regional Transit (ART) Rural Public Transportation
records.description_en: Shared-ride public transportation in rural areas, including curb-to-curb rides you book ahead and flex routes like Connect Seguin. Buses carry wheelchairs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public in the non-urban parts of the counties served, including Comal and Guadalupe.
records.how_to_apply: Call the ART reservation center at (866) 889-7433 (Mon-Fri 7 AM-6 PM) or email mobility@aacog.gov to book a ride.
records.cost: Demand response: $2 in town, $6 out of town in same county, $8 crossing one county line, $12 crossing two or more
records.notes: Serves non-urbanized areas of 12 counties. Flex-route deviations must be requested in advance.

records.name: Area Agency on Aging (Bexar and Alamo Region)
records.description_en: Helps adults 60+ with care coordination, help with utility bills, eyeglasses and dental needs, minor home repairs, emergency response systems, and free rides to medical and personal appointments.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults age 60 and older. Priority goes to seniors recovering from a major illness or hospital stay.
records.how_to_apply: Call the call center: Bexar County (210) 477-3275; Alamo Region, including Comal and Guadalupe, (866) 231-4922.
records.notes: Use (866) 231-4922 for Comal and Guadalupe. Email asc@aacog.gov. Senior transportation is free; other services depend on need.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Alamo Career Centers
records.description_en: Job search help, training, computer access, veterans services, youth programs, and vocational rehabilitation at career centers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers in the 13-county Alamo Region, including Bexar, Comal, and Guadalupe.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 224-4357 to find your nearest career center and career advisor.
records.notes: Local Texas Workforce Commission board. Main office line (210) 438-0581.

records.name: Child Care Services (Child Care Scholarships)
records.description_en: Scholarships that help eligible families pay for child care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Eligible families in the 13-county Alamo Region, including Bexar, Comal, and Guadalupe.
records.how_to_apply: Apply through Texas Child Care Connection (child care scholarships), or call Child Care Services.
records.notes: Toll-free 1-800-204-7905; email ccs@wsalamo.org.

records.name: City of San Antonio Head Start and Early Head Start
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Early learning programs: Early Head Start for babies 6 weeks to 35 months and Head Start for children 3 to 5.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children 6 weeks to 5 years old. Programs are in the Edgewood ISD and San Antonio ISD areas.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the ChildPlus application links on the Head Start website (English or Spanish), or call (210) 206-5500.
records.notes: Edgewood ISD line: (210) 898-2043; San Antonio ISD line: (210) 554-2410. Income limits not stated on the page.

records.name: The Center for Health Care Services (Bexar County Local Mental Health Authority)
records.organization: The Center for Health Care Services
records.description_en: Mental health care, substance use treatment, intellectual and developmental disability services, and 24-hour crisis help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People in Bexar County who need mental health, substance use, or IDD services.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-833-501-2427 for routine appointments. In a crisis, call (210) 223-7233 any time.
records.hours: Crisis and substance use helpline: 24 hours
records.notes: Crisis also at 1-800-316-9241. Routine appointments: 1-833-501-2427.

records.name: Hill Country MHDD Centers - Comal County Mental Health
records.organization: Hill Country Mental Health & Developmental Disabilities Centers
records.description_en: Local mental health authority for Comal County: mental health, substance use, crisis, IDD, child, and veteran services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Residents of the counties served, including Comal.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Comal County Mental Health office at (830) 620-6221. In a crisis call 1-877-466-0660.
records.notes: Crisis line 1-877-466-0660. Comal County LIDDA (IDD services): 358 Landa St, Suite 100, (830) 625-7394. Also clinics in Bulverde and Canyon Lake: (830) 387-5995.

records.name: Bluebonnet Trails Community Services - Seguin
records.description_en: Local mental health authority for Guadalupe County: mental health, substance use, crisis, IDD, autism, early childhood intervention, and supportive housing and employment.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Residents of the counties served, including Guadalupe.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-844-309-6385 for appointments or information. In a crisis call 1-800-841-1255 any time.

records.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid (TRLA) - San Antonio
records.description_en: Free civil legal help with housing and eviction, public benefits, family law, employment, disasters, and more.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income residents of 68 Southwest Texas counties, including Bexar, Comal, and Guadalupe.
records.how_to_apply: Call the hotline at (956) 996-8752, Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM. For family law, call only on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
records.notes: Apply by phone. San Antonio office address is from TRLA's offices page.

records.name: CentroMed Community Health Centers
records.description_en: Community health centers with family medicine, pediatrics, women's health, dental, pharmacy, and help applying for coverage.
records.eligibility_summary_en: You may qualify for a sliding fee based on income and family size. No one is turned away for inability to pay.
documents_needed: Proof of income
Family size information
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 922-7000 for an appointment. For sliding fee or payment help, call (210) 334-3745 to meet an eligibility specialist.
records.hours: Appointment line: Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-5:00 PM (24/7 support, option 3 after hours)
records.notes: Federally funded health center. Also has a pediatrics clinic at 955 Loop 337, New Braunfels 78130.

records.name: CentroMed WIC
records.description_en: WIC gives healthy foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5 who qualify.
records.how_to_apply: Call (210) 924-6004 or text (855) 441-0537 to schedule an appointment.
records.notes: Second WIC site: 5255 Walzem Road, San Antonio 78218.

records.name: Metro Health WIC Clinics
records.description_en: WIC nutrition program with healthy foods and support at clinics across San Antonio.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women, infants, and children younger than 5.
records.how_to_apply: Call 3-1-1 or (210) 207-6000, or see WIC Clinic Locations on the Metro Health WIC page.
records.notes: Clinic addresses and hours are on the linked clinic locations page (not confirmed here).

records.name: CommuniCare Health Centers
records.description_en: Primary care for all ages, dental, behavioral health, pharmacy, women's health, and WIC, with a sliding fee discount for those who qualify.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to all. Sliding fee discount for families with income under 200% of federal poverty guidelines.
documents_needed: Photo ID
Insurance card (if any)
List of medications
For sliding fee: proof of identity, income, and residency
records.how_to_apply: New patients call (210) 233-7000. For sliding fee questions call Medical Eligibility Specialists at (210) 233-7076.
records.notes: Sliding fee enrollment lasts one year. Serves Bexar, Kendall, Hays, and Comal counties; a New Braunfels clinic was listed as opening May 2026.

records.name: CareLink Financial Assistance
records.description_en: Makes care at University Health more affordable for uninsured Bexar County families. It is not insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Bexar County residents with income at or below 250% of federal poverty guidelines who do not have or qualify for health insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Complete the CareLink Enrollment Application online or call CareLink Member Services at (210) 358-3350.

records.name: Comal County Indigent Health Care Program
records.description_en: Covers doctor visits, tests, specialist care with referral, urgent and emergency care, and prescriptions for very low-income residents.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Comal County residents with income at or below 21% of federal poverty guidelines, resources under $2,000, and not eligible for Medicaid.
documents_needed: Completed Application for Service
Documents that verify income, resources, and residency
records.how_to_apply: Download the Application for Service (PDF) and call (830) 221-1210 for an appointment.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 8 AM-5 PM, by appointment only

records.name: Free Tax Preparation (VITA)
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Free income tax return preparation so families can get their full refund and tax credits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Individuals and families earning up to $60,000 a year.
documents_needed: Driver's license or photo ID
Social Security card or ITIN for all family members
All W-2 forms
If applicable: bank account numbers for direct deposit, prior year return, 1099-G, 1099-INT, 1099-R
records.how_to_apply: During tax season (mid-January to April) visit a VITA site; call 2-1-1 or visit vitasa.org for locations. The year-round clinic (May 1-Oct 30) needs an appointment: call (210) 207-6575.
records.notes: Alternate year-round clinic line: (210) 207-1712.

records.name: Financial Empowerment Center
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Free, private one-on-one financial counseling for banking, credit, debt, savings, and planning.
records.eligibility_summary_en: San Antonio and Bexar County residents 18 and older. No income limit.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: San Antonio or Bexar County resident

records.how_to_apply: Schedule an appointment online or call a center.
records.address: Willie Velasquez Center, 1302 N. Zarzamora St.
records.notes: Other sites: Claude Black Community Center, 2805 E. Commerce St., and The Neighborhood Place, 3014 Rivas St. (both (210) 431-4425).

records.name: Senior Congregate Meal Program (HEAL)
records.organization: City of San Antonio Department of Human Services
records.description_en: Meals, exercise, and social activities for older adults at city senior centers, with transportation services offered.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Older adults in San Antonio. The minimum age was not stated on the page.
records.how_to_apply: Enroll online through the city's senior registration portal (seniorstat4.net) and allow 2-3 business days, or call (210) 207-7172.
records.notes: 12 senior center locations are listed on the city site.
